question: Should OpenClaw accept SecretRefs for static `sandbox.docker.env` configuration, knowing the resolved values will be exposed through the same Docker container and daemon metadata boundary as existing literal environment variables?
rationale: The implementation is technically aligned with existing sandbox and SecretRef patterns, but whether SecretRefs should be supported at this Docker credential boundary is a product and security-policy choice rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Accept the existing Docker boundary
options.body: Merge the feature with its current fail-closed active-resolution behavior and keep the Docker metadata exposure warning explicit.

options.title: Keep Docker sandbox env literal-only
options.body: Decline this configuration surface and leave operators to use the currently supported literal or external deployment mechanisms.

options.title: Request a different secret-delivery design
options.body: Pause this PR for a design that avoids exposing resolved values through ordinary Docker environment metadata.

recommendation.title: Accept the existing Docker boundary
recommendation.body: Merge the feature with its current fail-closed active-resolution behavior and keep the Docker metadata exposure warning explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work defines both the existing Docker environment behavior and the runtime SecretRef resolution pattern this proposal extends.
